pages.text: NBT requirements are configured through $(bold)JSON files in datapacks$(). This means modpack developers can add, override, or remove NBT tracking without modifying the mod.

pages.title: Directory Structure
pages.text: data/   <namespace>/     nbt_requirements/       blocks/         $(italic).json     ← NBT requirements for placed blocks       items/         $().json     ← NBT requirements for inventory items$(br2)FPSCompress ships with: data/fpscompress/nbt_requirements/blocks/prefab.json

pages.title: JSON Format
pages.text: Each file defines NBT matching rules for a single resource:$(br2){   "resource_id": "modid:item_or_block_name",   "match": {     "path.to.field": "strategy",     "path.to.nested.field": {       "strategy": "strategy_name",       "ignore": ["transient_key"],       "min": 0.0,       "max": 100.0     }   } }$(br2)$(bold)`resource_id`$() (required): The namespaced registry ID of the block or item.$(br2)$(bold)`match`$() (required): A map of NBT paths to matching rules. Each path uses $(bold)dot notation$() (e.g., `"BlockEntityTag.roomCode"`). Use `$(italic)` as a wildcard for list element paths (e.g., `"importerExporterRates.$().rates"`).$(br2)#### Match Rule Formats$(br2)Each match value can be a $(bold)shorthand string$() or an $(bold)object$():$(br2)$(bold)String shorthand$() (simple cases): "path.to.field": "exact"$(br2)$(bold)Object form$() (with options): "path.to.field": {   "strategy": "list_subset",   "ignore": ["uuid", "timestamp"],   "min": 0.0,   "max": 100.0 }

pages.title: Match Strategies
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)`exact`:$() Values must match exactly - Simple fields (strings, numbers) $(li)$(bold)`subset`:$() Required fields must exist in available; extra fields in available are OK - Compound tags where you care about specific sub-fields $(li)$(bold)`list_subset`:$() Every element in the required list must have a match in the available list (order-independent) - Lists of items/rates where order doesn't matter $(li)$(bold)`range`:$() Numeric value must fall within `[min, max]` - Energy levels, durability, progress values$(br2)$(bold)Default behavior$(): If no match rule is specified for a path, compound tags use `subset` and primitive tags use `exact`.

pages.title: The `ignore` Field
pages.text: Use `ignore` to skip $(bold)transient$() or $(bold)volatile$() keys that differ between otherwise-identical items:$(br2){   "resource_id": "fpscompress:prefab_machine",   "match": {     "importerExporterRates": {       "strategy": "list_subset",       "ignore": ["uuid"]     }   } }$(br2)This says: "Compare `importerExporterRates` lists element-by-element, but skip the `uuid` field inside each element." UUIDs are assigned per-Importer/Exporter and differ between copies — ignoring them allows carbon copies to match.$(br2)Common things to ignore: $(li)`uuid` — Unique identifiers that differ per instance $(li)`timestamp` — Creation/modification times $(li)`x`, `y`, `z` — Block positions (differ between copies)

pages.title: Real Examples
pages.text: $(bold)Example 1: PreFab Block$() (shipped with the mod)$(br2)File: `data/fpscompress/nbt_requirements/blocks/prefab.json`$(br2){   "resource_id": "fpscompress:prefab_machine",   "match": {     "importerExporterRates": {       "strategy": "list_subset",       "ignore": ["uuid"]     },     "importerExporterRates.*.rates": "list_subset"   } }$(br2)This ensures: $(li)The `importerExporterRates` list in a printed PreFab must match the blueprint's rates element-by-element $(li)UUIDs are ignored (carbon copies get new UUIDs for their own Importers/Exporters) $(li)The inner `rates` sub-list within each entry also uses `list_subset` matching$(br2)$(bold)Example 2: Enchanted Book$() (hypothetical — add via datapack)$(br2)File: `data/minecraft/nbt_requirements/items/enchanted_book.json`$(br2){   "resource_id": "minecraft:enchanted_book",   "match": {     "StoredEnchantments": "list_subset"   } }$(br2)Ensures a blueprint requiring an Efficiency V book won't accept a Sharpness III book.$(br2)$(bold)Example 3: Machine with Upgrades$() (hypothetical — add via datapack)$(br2)File: `data/examplemod/nbt_requirements/blocks/super_furnace.json`$(br2){   "resource_id": "examplemod:super_furnace",   "match": {     "BlockEntityTag.Upgrades.SpeedTier": "exact",     "BlockEntityTag.Upgrades.EfficiencyTier": "exact",     "BlockEntityTag.EnergyStored": {       "strategy": "range",       "min": 0.0,       "max": 1000000.0     }   } }$(br2)Ensures blueprints require matching speed/efficiency upgrade tiers but accepts any energy level (as long as it's within the machine's capacity).$(br2)---
